config.title: Build typed task scheduler interface

intro.title: Build typed task scheduler interface
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a typed task scheduler interface using TypeScript. You will create a simple system to manage tasks with priorities and due dates, ensuring type safety throughout. The core concept is using TypeScript interfaces to define the shape of your data, preventing errors by specifying types for task properties. You'll work with basic TypeScript constructs like interfaces, type annotations, and optional properties. By the end, you'll have a functional, type-safe interface that can be used to schedule and organize tasks in a structured way.
intro.usecase: Typed task scheduler interfaces are essential in productivity applications like project management tools (e.g., Asana, Trello) where users create, prioritize, and track tasks with deadlines and statuses. They also power background job systems in web applications that handle scheduled email campaigns, report generation, or data synchronization with strict type safety. In developer tools, typed schedulers manage build pipelines, automated testing queues, and deployment workflows where each task has specific parameters and return types. This pattern ensures reliability in complex scheduling scenarios like calendar applications, cron job managers, and workflow automation platforms where tasks must be validated at compile time.

objectives: Implement a TypeScript interface to define the structure of a task scheduler
Apply generic types to create a flexible task scheduler that handles different data types
Construct a class that implements the task scheduler interface with proper type annotations
Initialize a task scheduler instance with typed configuration options
Manipulate task arrays using type-safe methods for adding, removing, and filtering tasks
Integrate type guards to validate task statuses and ensure runtime type safety
Render a formatted task list by mapping over typed task objects with proper property access
